newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. directs state to pay Calpers $1.36 bln.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. directs state to pay Calpers $1.36 bln.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Tuesday directed the state to immediately repay the California Public Employees' Retirement System (Calpers) an estimated $1.36 billion for funds the state used to balance its budgets in the early 1990s.
Wilson, a Republican, told state Controller Kathleen Connell, a Democrat, to cut the check as soon as possible.

Wilson said by repaying Calpers immediately, the state would save $650 million in interest over 10 years, plus $1.5 billion in expanded retirement benefits demanded by the pension system's board of directors.
Wilson and state Democrats had hoped to pay the money back over several years.
Wilson said that Calpers was "unwilling to offer an affordable" repayment plan, forcing the state to pay the money back in a lump sum out of its 1997-1998 budget.

A state appeals court ruled in February that the governor and the legislature improperly withheld the money from Calpers in the early 1990s to balance state budgets during California's deepest economic downturn since the Depression.
In May, the state Supreme Court refused to rehear the case.
Wilson said repaying Calpers would require lawmakers to curtail their spending plans for fiscal year 1997-1998.
Funding for Wilson's proposed business tax cut would be eliminated, and money for most other non-education programs could be threatened, the governor said.
Wilson said education funding would not suffer.
Wilson urged Connell to quickly reimburse Calpers.
"She would be unwise not to do it," the governor told reporters. "Now is her opportunity to shine."
